title: 8 Zeros? Scientific Notation Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Light covers about 300 million metres every second, and a hydrogen atom is about one ten-billionth of a metre wide. Aarav tries to write the speed of light with all its zeros and loses count. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn the trick physicists use: scientific notation.

On a live notation bench the decimal point hops left and right while a graph tracks the power of ten. We write any number as a x 10^b with 1 <= a < 10, see why big numbers get positive powers and small numbers get negative ones, and find the order of magnitude of the earth (1.28 x 10^7 m) and the hydrogen atom (1.06 x 10^-10 m), as given in NCERT. Then a worked example (sunlight takes about 500 s to reach us), the exam trap about the sign of the power, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Huge numbers, tiny numbers
0:30 The form: a front number times a power of ten
0:48 The notation bench: hop the decimal point
1:20 The hydrogen atom: negative powers
1:40 The rule, step by step
2:07 Side by side + pause and think
2:44 Order of magnitude
3:36 Worked example: how old is sunlight?
4:13 Exam trap: the sign of the power
4:38 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:22 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Accuracy and Precision. A scale that gives the same reading every time, but is wrong: accurate or precise?
